transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Omar, Priya (Redwood); Liam, Zara, Marcus, Anika (Equinox)

Auto-summary (auto gen may be rough): quick partner intro; agree pilot; check GPU and network; ask for SOC2 docs; schedule follow-up.

[00:00:12] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, account lead on partnerships. Omar and Priya are our SE and solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:00:20] Liam: Good, thanks. Quick intro from Equinox side — I'm Liam, I run partnerships, and Zara is our cloud lead. Marcus is our CTO, and Anika is on security.
[00:00:33] Zara: Hi all. Excited to explore this, we've been looking for a smoother onramp for customers to spin up inference at the edge.
[00:00:40] Omar: Awesome. To set context, Redwood provides a unified inference runtime — hosted, dedicated, or private — that we've optimized for low-latency and cost controls. Today we'd like to understand Equinox's architecture and see where we fit.
[00:00:55] Marcus: Quick note — our differentiator is an edge onramp that pre-provisions GPU-capable nodes in partner colo sites. We want to offer our customers a drop-in inference runtime. Key questions: kernel compatibility, footprint for KV cache, and how data residency and network egress would work.
[00:01:12] Priya: When you say KV cache, you mean the key-value KV for autoregressive models? We often expose prefix caching that reduces per-token compute. How are you planning to manage model state across nodes?
[00:01:25] Zara: Right, we have a shared object-store plus local NVMe on nodes. We can host K V cache locally, but we'd like Redwood to confirm cache warming behavior and expected disk footprint per model.
[00:01:36] Omar: Understood. For our runtime we typically measure KV state in hundreds of megabytes for medium-size models, larger for context windows >8k. We also provide optional shared KV layer across a small cluster — but that'll depend on network latency.
[00:01:47] Marcus: Network latency is the big unknown. Our edge sites sometimes have 10–30ms to the core region; some are 50+. If the runtime expects low latency to a central caching layer that could be a problem.
[00:01:58] Maya: That's a useful data point. A couple options: 1) run Redwood Private locally (on-prem package) at the site, 2) deploy a lightweight dedicated agent that holds KV cache, or 3) route requests to a nearby dedicated pool. Tradeoffs are cost vs velocity.
[00:02:12] Liam: From a partnership point-of-view we care about margin and how easy the integration is for our customers. If Redwood can offer a small footprint on our nodes and a simple onboarding flow, that's ideal.
[00:02:21] Anika: Security questions: we need SOC 2 attestation, details about encryption-at-rest, KMS integration, and SSO (SAML/Okta) support. Also audit logs and RBAC.
[00:02:33] Priya: Totally. We have a security pack we can share — includes SOC 2 report, details on KMS/HSM options, SAML support, and audit log retention defaults. We'll add that to the follow-up packet.
[00:02:45] Zara: Great. Also, do you support pinning model versions and automatic fallback to quantized variants? We have customers sensitive to output quality.
[00:02:55] Omar: Yes — we support version pinning and rollout policies. For fallback, our routing can detect overload and fall back to a quantized or smaller model variant. The key is balancing latency and quality. Often quantization reduces memory and cost but can change response characteristics.
[00:03:12] Marcus: We run many LLMs, some custom. How's model onboarding? Do you accept ONNX, GGML, or do you ingest open model formats?
[00:03:21] Priya: We ingest several formats. Our onboarding engine prefers standard model checkpoints and will convert or compile models into runtime-optimized kernels. We do have a small set of supported quantized formats — team will share the exact list.
[00:03:33] Liam: Pilot idea: can Redwood run a 48-hour benchmark against one of our test edge sites using a small model and then expand? We'd want latency P95, cost estimates, and a rough integration checklist.
[00:03:45] Maya: Yes, that's straightforward. Omar can run the benchmark with your test cluster credentials or via a partner VM. We'd aim to capture P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and cold vs warm start differences.
[00:03:56] Omar: Quick note — for kernel compatibility, A100 and H100 have different optimal kernels. We should check which GPUs you have in your colo. Also, if you intend to use FP16 vs 4-bit quant, that changes memory profiles.
[00:04:08] Zara: Most of our sites are A100, a few newer ones H100. We also support some RTX-class for smaller customers.
[00:04:16] Marcus: Costing — our customers will ask: hosted API vs dedicated vs private. Can you outline the high-level economic tradeoffs?
[00:04:24] Maya: Sure. Hosted API is fastest to market; you pay per-token and get Redwood-managed infra. Dedicated is reserved capacity — predictable throughput and better unit economics at scale. Private/VPC gives you control and data residency but involves onboarding and an infra license. We'll share a one-pager with example numbers.
[00:04:40] Anika: About data residency — some customers require logs not leave the tenant network. Does Redwood support on-prem private control plane?
[00:04:47] Priya: Yes, our Private deployment allows a customer-managed control plane and can be run in a VPC or on-prem with HSM/KMS integrations. Audit logs can be retained inside your environment depending on deployment mode.
[00:04:58] Liam: From go-to-market, we're thinking channel/reseller. What partner motions do you support — referral, resale, co-sell?
[00:05:06] Maya: We support multiple motions. Typical early partners start as referral/integration partners, then pilot reseller or white-label options. We also have partner enablement docs and a partner portal. We'll send the partner handbook excerpt.
[00:05:16] Zara: Can you share sample API calls and SDK examples? We want to embed it into our onboarding flow.
[00:05:22] Omar: Absolutely — we'll provide SDK snippets for Python/Go and sample streaming responses. Note: streaming and function calling are supported, but there are trade-offs when you route through proxies or edge load balancers.
[00:05:33] Marcus: One technical thing — how do you handle autoscaling at the edge? Horizontal spin-up times could be long.
[00:05:40] Priya: We recommend pre-warmed pools for edge use cases. For autoscaling, there's also burst capacity options, but at the edge pre-warm and small-scale pooling gives the best latency SLOs.
[00:05:51] Anika: For compliance, can you provide details about retention policies for logs and user prompts? Some enterprise customers need 30/90 day retention and deletion controls.
[00:05:59] Maya: Yes, retention is configurable; for Hosted we have defaults, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies and request deletion flows. We'll include those details in the security packet.
[00:06:10] Liam: Any blockers from your side for a pilot?
[00:06:13] Omar: We need access to a test node or VM, GPU type details, and a rough traffic profile. Also, a point of contact for infra access.
[00:06:20] Zara: We can provide a test VM with A100 and synthetic traffic. I'll share those details after the meeting.
[00:06:26] Maya: Great. Let's try to keep timeline: spec + docs by Thu, pilot kickoff next week, legal to start NDA today. Sound OK?
[00:06:35] Marcus: Works for us.
[00:06:37] Anika: I'll loop legal and security, expect an initial email.
[00:06:40] Priya: One more technical aside — quantization impacts latency differently across kernels; we'll prepare a small matrix showing expected memory and latency for FP16 vs 8-bit vs 4-bit for your common models.
[00:06:51] Omar: Also, note GPU sharing: if you plan multi-tenant usage on a node, we recommend container isolation plus enforced cgroups to control GPU memory; otherwise KV cache thrashing can occur.
[00:07:04] Zara: Good point — we run multi-tenant in some sites. We'll need guidance on isolation patterns.
[00:07:10] Maya: We'll document recommended shapes and isolation configs.
[00:07:14] Liam: For commercial: rough margin expectations for partners?
[00:07:19] Maya: We can propose partner pricing tiers. Typically partners get a discounted resell margin and we co-invest on initial pilots in some cases. We'll include an indicative pricing sheet.
[00:07:28] [crosstalk, brief laugh]
[00:07:33] Omar: Anything else?
[00:07:36] Marcus: No, that's good. Appreciate the quick clarifications.
[00:07:40] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs pack and calendar invite for the SE deep-dive.
[00:07:46] Liam: Thanks, talk soon.

Meeting end.
